title: DEPS — Alpha Explicit Allowlist Disclosure Producer Shadow

sprint.name: Alpha Explicit Allowlist Disclosure Producer Shadow
sprint.classification: B — Producer Contract Valid; Identity or Durable Access Integration Required
sprint.scope: Inactive request-time Alpha allowlist decision production, authorization-before-Runtime orchestration, exact authority validation, audit-ready output, and end-to-end delivery replay.

evidence.claimBoundary: Sixty-one deterministic identity, access, preflight, loader-isolation, authority, revocation, audit, delivery-chain, Runtime non-mutation, and active-route isolation checks.
Pure request-time policy contracts with injected access reader and Runtime loader; no production identity, persistence, route, or network integration.
Architecture, threat results, validation hashes, activation dependencies, rollback, Scorecard limits, and next recommendation.
Existing fourteen-check disclosure and revocation contract regression.
Existing sixty-nine-check inactive Your Organization communication adapter regression.
Existing twenty-four-check active product and persisted replay regression.

scorecard.rationale: The producer validates access and authority references without creating, ranking, revising, or persisting organizational cognition.
The shadow is inactive and uses benchmark-owned identity; no real-user comprehension or decision outcome was measured.
No contribution, collaboration, membership, cross-scope use, or shared learning behavior changed.

The inactive shadow now demonstrates explicit identity and access inputs, default-deny preflight before Runtime loading, exact authority validation, request-time revocation, and audit-ready provenance.
Typed identity, access-reader, preflight, loader, decision, and audit boundaries isolate the transitional policy and preserve a local rollback.

architecture.observation: Denied, revoked, invalid, guessed, and reader-failure cases cannot invoke the injected Runtime loader.
The Alpha policy produces the existing resolved decision while existing disclosure enforcement remains the filtering owner.
Clerk verification and durable access and audit stores remain absent; hosted activation is blocked.
No route or UI imports the producer and active Phase 8A behavior remains unchanged.

benchmarks.summary: The inactive producer is deterministic, explicit, request-bound, fail-closed, authorization-before-Runtime, authority-exact, audit-ready, and end-to-end delivery compatible.
The disclosed projection boundary remains passing.
The structured communication contract remains passing.
The inactive product communication adapter remains passing.
The active Runtime-backed experience remains unchanged.

researchObservations.observation: No research adapter, Local Understanding Utility profile, nonlinear cognition, or production-readiness conclusion changed.

introduced: One isolated Alpha governance producer module with typed identity, access, receipt, preflight, decision, audit, and orchestration contracts.
One focused sixty-one-check validator with a benchmark-owned identity, access reader, audit sink, and persisted Runtime replay.
One measurement source and versioned DEPS report.
complexity.justification: The additions prove the minimum fail-closed authorization boundary and full inactive delivery chain without coupling policy to Runtime, routes, projection, communication, or UI.

governanceObservations.observation: Explicit request-time access, revocation, authority, provenance, and denial behavior now have a deterministic inactive implementation boundary.

sustainabilityObservations.observation: The policy is isolated behind injected interfaces, normalized identities, deterministic IDs, no cross-request cache, no persistence, and an exact removal boundary.

regressions.observation: The producer remains inactive; active route and UI behavior are unchanged.
Persisted Atlas Runtime is byte-identical before and after replay.

unknownsAndUnmeasured.reason: No user-visible treatment, comprehension study, or decision outcome changed.
The typed identity is constructed only by the benchmark; Clerk is not installed or integrated.
Injected records and an in-memory append-only-shaped sink do not demonstrate durable lifecycle, operations, or incident recovery.
No route, deployment, browser session, or operational activation was attempted.

remainingRisks.nextBlockingDependency: Actual server-verified Clerk identity must construct the typed consumer identity before durable access records can bind to a real principal.
remainingRisks.remainingDiscoveryPhase: Phase 8 shadows remain inactive; broader Phase 5 Governance and Phase 6 remain paused.
remainingRisks.remainingBenchmarkGap: Real provider identity, durable access and audit lifecycle, browser isolation, operational failure handling, and activation rollback remain unmeasured.

rollback.description: Remove the producer, validator, command, DEPS source/report, and documentation synchronization; Runtime, cognition, disclosure enforcement, projection, communication, routes, UI, dependencies, and persisted organizations remain unchanged.

engineeringDecision.rationale: Accept the inactive producer shadow and make actual Clerk identity integration in shadow the one next separately authorized step. Hosted activation remains blocked.
